properties.name: Design information lives in the graph, not in documents
properties.statement:
This project does not store design information in documents. What a document would have said belongs in the graph as typed nodes. Anthony's word, 2026-08-15: "we no longer use documents to store info. should be in graph" — and, on the buildup of two feedback files captured only partially, "we can't let this buildup occur again".

ENFORCEMENT IS HIS EXPLICIT ANSWER, NOT AN INHERITED DEFAULT. Asked what should happen if somebody added a markdown file holding design information — good content, tests passing — he chose STOP THE BUILD over advice and over leaving it unstated.

═══ WHY, IN HIS WORDS (2026-08-15, the reasoning behind the rule) ═══

THREE ARGUMENTS, and each has a measured precedent in this project or a neighbouring one:

(1) DOCUMENTS GET FORGOTTEN AND ARE HARD TO MAINTAIN. His example is this project's own: "like our initial backlog file of tasks for reflow2 kept growing and growing". That is `dec:backlog-is-retired` — 218 rows and 592 KB before it was retired into the graph on 2026-08-07, with an accepted decision violated and re-derived three times in the session that finally fixed it.

(2) A CORPUS OF THEM PILES UP FASTER THAN ANYONE READS IT. "what scared me was a corpus of feedback docs piling up. In dev_storyflow, I think I had 900+ documents of records that we're now having to go through slowly." The fear is not the first document; it is the nine hundredth, and the fact that the reading debt arrives long after the writing felt free.

(3) A DOCUMENT IS NOT SEARCHABLE THE WAY THE GRAPH IS. "documents are external and require grep to see contents (assuming markdown files, but that isn't always the case) — having in the graph is immediately searchable." The parenthesis is the sharp part: `search_design` works on any node, while grep only works on text formats, and a PDF, a spreadsheet or a drawing is opaque to it entirely.

═══ THE EXCEPTION HE STATED, WHICH SCOPES THE RULE ═══

⭐ "unless they are like a manual for using the designed system". THAT IS THE LINE: a document that is a DELIVERABLE OF the designed system — a user manual, an operator's guide — is not design information and this rule does not reach it. What the rule forbids is design information ABOUT the system living outside the graph.

⭐ AND A CONCESSION HE OFFERED UNPROMPTED: "If there was a way to put a pointer in the graph to the external document, that might be okay, but I think it is cleaner if we don't have external docs." A pointer is `Artifact.location` and `Fragment.content_ref`, both of which already exist and are exactly that — so the concession is already implementable, and he is stating a PREFERENCE for cleanliness over it rather than a prohibition on it.

═══ THE COUNTER HE RAISED AGAINST HIMSELF ═══

"The counter in some ways is something like dev_storyflow that did maintain a lot of records of the design." Recorded because he raised it and because it cuts: the same 900+ documents that are now a reading debt are also a design record that survived, and no graph held it at the time.

═══ THE LIMIT HE NAMED, AND IT IS THE REAL BOUNDARY ═══

From the acquisition world he works in: "in some designs, actual design reviews are done and official direction to proceed and other formal docs are required (coming from the US Air Force and US Space Force, documentation is required — maybe we can eventually get to where the graph tracks authorizations to proceed or other official acquisitions documents are in the graph and organizations trust the graph to hold such docs and therefore, keeping external docs is no longer needed — but I don't think we are there yet)."

SO THE RULE IS STATED FOR THIS PROJECT AND IS NOT YET CLAIMED TO GENERALISE. Whether reflow2 could become the system of record an organisation trusts for formal authorisation is open in `dec:idea-can-the-graph-be-the-official-record-an-organisation-trusts`, recorded separately because it is a question about the product rather than a rule about this repository.

⚠️ THIS RULE OWES A DETECTOR AND CANNOT HAVE ONE YET, because two things must be scoped before a check could tell a violation from ordinary work:

(1) SCOPE. 187 markdown files are tracked outside `docs/design/`. AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, COORD.md, REFLOW2.md, README, CHANGELOG and every served SKILL.md are documents, and several are load-bearing instructions the project cannot function without. The manual exception above narrows this but does not settle it: served SKILL.md files are closer to "a manual for using the designed system" than to design information, and nobody has ruled.

(2) A CONFLICT WITH THE SCHEMA'S OWN DESIGN, measured 2026-08-15: `Fragment.content_ref` is "a pointer to the source content RATHER THAN INLINING IT", and Fragment carries no field for a document's text. `Artifact.location` and `DOCUMENTS` share that assumption. AND THE FEATURE THAT WOULD HAVE CLOSED IT WAS BUILT AND WITHDRAWN: `cap:content-store` held "the source documents a corpus was extracted from", was `realized` and verified, and was discontinued on his word on 2026-08-09 for zero use across three projects (`dec:the-content-store-is-discontinued`). That discontinuation left `req:sources-are-kept-not-just-parsed` accepted and unsatisfied ON PURPOSE, with a `design_artifacts` folder — a folder of documents — named as the intended replacement and still unbuilt. THIS RULE AND THAT REQUIREMENT CURRENTLY POINT IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, six days apart, both on his word.
